name: Holy See (Vatican City State)

findings.controller: Microsoft (AI for Good Lab processed the imagery with AI)
findings.local_actor: Fabric of Saint Peter (Fabbrica di San Pietro)
findings.summary: The Fabric of Saint Peter and Microsoft launched an AI-built digital twin of St Peter's Basilica from Iconem's 2023 imagery capture, used for virtual visits and to map cracks and missing mosaic tiles for conservation.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole us because Microsoft supplied the AI processing; hosting of the 3D model and websites (basilicasanpietro.va) is undisclosed, so whether Microsoft retains operational control after delivery is unknown. Described as a collaboration; no contract, value or ownership terms published. Tier 5 because the product was delivered and launched, but this is a single-building cultural project, not a state stack commitment.

findings.controller: Governorate of Vatican City State, Directorate of Telecommunications and Information Systems
findings.summary: The Governorate's telecoms and IT director said state data are stored and processed in data centres inside Vatican territory, with more server clusters planned and data-centre areas being engineered to host AI solutions on-premise.
findings.analyst_inference: Single S1 source (the Holy See's own outlet describing its own infrastructure). No hardware, AI or model vendors are named; the 'AI ready' on-premise hosting is a plan, not an observed deployment, and is not separately coded.

findings.local_actor: Vatican Apostolic Library (IT director Luciano Ammenti)
findings.builder: Panduit (US), racks, cabling and monitoring gateways
findings.summary: The Vatican Apostolic Library replaced its obsolete data centre using Panduit racks with hot-aisle containment, fibre and copper cabling and monitoring gateways, supporting digitisation of its collections.
findings.analyst_inference: Owner-operator is the Library, so domestic; Panduit supplied largely passive physical infrastructure and is recorded as builder. Single opened S2 source; pre-2020 and current status not confirmed.

findings.local_actor: TIM (Telecom Italia); Vodafone Italia in progress
findings.summary: Italian operator TIM completed 5G mobile coverage of Vatican territory in 2025, according to the Governorate's IT director; Vodafone 5G coverage was still in progress and Castel Gandolfo coverage was being designed.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: under the equipment-vendor rule the controller is TIM's radio/core vendor for the Vatican sites, which no source names. Source treated as S4 because it is a Holy See outlet describing a third party's network. An October 2020 ITU profile (opened) said no 5G had launched in the Vatican and fibre links connect to an unnamed Italian operator.

findings.local_actor: Gendarmerie Corps of Vatican City State
findings.summary: Israeli firm ioimage's intelligent-video cameras and encoders, installed from 2005 via integrator Picksec, monitor about 60 km of sensitive perimeter, gates and walls from the Vatican Gendarmerie control room for intruder detection.
findings.analyst_inference: Both opened sources appear to reproduce the same vendor press release (same facts and integrator quote), so they are not independent and corroboration is false. Pre-2020; current use not confirmed.

findings.local_actor: Gendarmerie Corps of Vatican City State; Vatican Museums
findings.summary: A Panasonic CCTV system of 556 cameras on a dedicated fibre network, run by the Gendarmerie, covered the Vatican site, with a separate Vatican Museums control room using video analytics and Panasonic recorders.
findings.analyst_inference: Single S2 trade-press source from a Panasonic-organised press trip. Pre-2020 (2007); whether Panasonic equipment is still in service is unknown.

silicon.null_reason: no accelerator purchase or deployment surfaced; the Governorate interview names no hardware vendor for planned on-premise AI hosting

models.null_reason: Governorate AI Guidelines (end 2024) and AI proofs of concept found, but no named model provider, partnership or sovereign model; Rome Call for AI Ethics is a non-binding ethics pledge, not stack adoption

research_gaps: Which AI products or model providers were used in the Governorate's AI proofs of concept and planned on-premise AI hosting (Feb 2026 interview names none).
Radio/core equipment vendor for TIM's (2025) and Vodafone's 5G coverage of Vatican territory and Castel Gandolfo.
Current Gendarmerie CCTV/video-analytics vendor; whether the 2005-2008 ioimage and 2007 Panasonic systems remain in service and whether any PRC camera brands were introduced since.
Hosting/cloud provider and data-ownership terms for the St Peter's Basilica digital twin and basilicasanpietro.va sites (Azure or other).

Microsoft's ties with the Holy See beyond the Rome Call for AI Ethics (a non-binding pledge, not coded; CNS dates Microsoft-Vatican work from 2018): any service or licence agreements beyond the basilica project.
NTT Data's earlier digitisation/archive partnership with the Vatican Apostolic Library (seen only as a search-result title, not opened) and where the archive is hosted.
